items.note: From ctl #1390. items.text:
Trusted mail between agents. Speaks as one endpoint.

Usage: mash <command> [options]

SAP is the Synadia Agent Protocol, NATS is the message server mash
talks to, and creds are the file that signs an endpoint in to it.

Everyday:
  mash send <address> [<message>] [options]    Send a message to an endpoint.
  mash inbox [options]                         List the messages this endpoint
                                               has received.
  mash read <number>                           Show one message in full.
  mash who [<prefix>] [options]                List the endpoints you can see,
                                               and which are online.
  mash status                                  Say in one line whether mail
                                               works for this endpoint, and
                                               whether it is online.
  mash doctor [options]                        Check everything mail depends on
                                               for this endpoint, and say how to
                                               fix what is wrong. Changes
                                               nothing.
  mash version                                 Print the version. It can also be
                                               run as --version.

Setup:
  mash join <file> [options]                   Install an endpoint's credentials
                                               on this machine from a join file.
  mash key create [options]                    Make your own key pair, for when
                                               the seed must never leave this
                                               machine.

Integration:
  mash serve [options]                         Run as an MCP server for an agent
                                               host. Started by the host, not by
                                               hand.
  mash hook                                    Print mail waiting for this
                                               session, in the form the agent
                                               host expects. Run by the host
                                               after each tool call and with
                                               each prompt.

Raw SAP:
  mash prompt <address> <text>                 Ask an endpoint a live question
                                               and wait for its answer. Not
                                               stored: if the recipient is not
                                               there, it fails.

Global options:
  --endpoint <address>  Which endpoint to act as, as owner.group.name. Not
                        needed for the everyday and setup commands when only one
                        is installed here. mash serve and mash hook always need
                        it said: a session becomes an endpoint only because
                        someone chose that.
  --creds <path>        The creds file to sign in with. Default: <config
                        folder>/<address>.creds.
  --server <url>        The server address. May be given more than once.
  --ca <path>           The certificate authority's certificate, when the server
                        uses its own.
  --config-dir <path>   The configuration folder. Default: ~/.config/mash.
  --detail              Print the fuller answer: after the usual line, more as
                        'label: value' lines; with --json, the fuller object.
  --json                Print the result as JSON: the same object the matching
                        MCP tool returns.
  --no-color            Never use color. Color is used only on a terminal, and
                        NO_COLOR is honored.
  -h, --help            Show help for the command.

An endpoint is addressed owner.group.name: MASH_ENDPOINT (or config.json
"endpoint", or --endpoint). With none set, the one endpoint whose creds file
(owner.group.name.creds, mode 0600) is in the config directory is used; with
several, name one.
A global option may stand anywhere in the command. A flag beats its environment
variable, which beats config.json.
Configuration: config.json {"servers","endpoint","ca"} in $MASH_CONFIG_DIR
(default ~/.config/mash, or $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mash), overridden by MASH_SERVER
(commas between several), MASH_ENDPOINT, MASH_CA, MASH_CREDS, MASH_ADMIN_CREDS,
MASH_HOST (see docs/install.md).
State (spool, hook.log): $MASH_STATE_DIR (default $XDG_STATE_HOME/mash, else
~/.local/state/mash).
Slow link: "open_timeout" (default 20s) and "call_timeout" (default 15s), or
MASH_OPEN_TIMEOUT and MASH_CALL_TIMEOUT.
Also tunable: lease_retry, transient_budget, transient_max, cli_timeout,
admin_timeout (MASH_LEASE_RETRY, MASH_TRANSIENT_BUDGET, MASH_TRANSIENT_MAX,
MASH_CLI_TIMEOUT, MASH_ADMIN_TIMEOUT).

Run mash <command> --help for a command's options.
items.note: Layout change only, per the rule "--help has one layout". (1) A Usage: line after the description, in the same one-line form mashctl --help uses: Usage: mash <command> [options]. Today there is none. (2) One footer as the last line, after the configuration text and a blank line: Run mash <command> --help for a command's options. mashctl --help ends with the same sentence naming mashctl (mashctl endpoint --help already ends Run mashctl endpoint <command> --help for a command's options.). A docs URL does not fit the footer in 80 columns, so it is not in it. Built on the planned text of help-mash-top (its one-sentence glossary); item help-mash-top-glossary adds the longer glossary on top of this. Today: no Usage line, no footer.

items.text:
Usage: mashctl <verb> [args]

SAP is the Synadia Agent Protocol, NATS is the message server mash
talks to, and creds are the file that signs an endpoint in to it.

  mashctl init --config path [--dry-run] [--json]
      set mash up on a NATS server you already have, from a setup file; safe to
      run again
  mashctl status [--json]
      one line per server: whether it works, how many endpoints it has, how many
      are online
  mashctl limits show [--json]
      print the limits in force
  mashctl doctor [--strict] [--json]
      check the server, mash's storage on it and every endpoint's records, and
      say how to fix what is wrong; changes nothing
  mashctl limits apply [prefix] [--dry-run] [--json]
      raise existing inboxes to the configured limits (never lowers); prefix is
      an owner, owner.group or one address
  mashctl endpoint list [prefix] [--wide] [--json]
      the endpoints in the directory
  mashctl endpoint show <address> [--json]
      one endpoint: its state, labels and public key
  mashctl endpoint create <address> [--out PATH] [--public-key PATH] [--dry-run]
          [--json]
      make an endpoint and its credentials, for example acme.demo.bob
  mashctl endpoint reissue <address> [--out PATH] [--public-key PATH]
          [--dry-run] [--json]
      give an endpoint new credentials and cancel the old ones
  mashctl endpoint delete <address> [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json]
      revoke the endpoint's user key, remove its record and inbox, burn the
      address, rename its creds file
  mashctl endpoint set <address> key=value... [--dry-run] [--json]
      set role, description, host, capability or label.NAME
  mashctl endpoint unset <address> key... [--dry-run] [--json]
      remove those values
  mashctl endpoint suspend <address> [--json]
      refuse new mail to an endpoint; its stored mail and credentials stay
  mashctl endpoint resume <address> [--json]
      take new mail again, undoing suspend
  mashctl endpoint inbox <address> [--after number] [--limit n] [--json]
      what is in an endpoint's inbox, without any message text
  mashctl endpoint permissions <address> [--json]
      the NATS permissions an endpoint's user needs
  mashctl version [--json]
      print the version and the commit

Global options (before or after the verb):
  --server <url>       The server address. May be given more than once.
  --creds <path>       The administrator's creds file.
  --ca <path>          The certificate authority's certificate, when the
                       server uses its own.
  --config-dir <path>  The configuration folder. Default: ~/.config/mash.
  --detail             Print the fuller answer: after the usual line, more as
                       'label: value' lines; with --json, the fuller object.
  --json               Print the result as JSON.
  --no-color           Never use color.
  -h, --help           Show help for the command.

Run mashctl <command> --help for a command's options.
items.note: help-mashctl-top's planned text with three changes and nothing else. (1) usage: becomes Usage: (capital U, as mash). (2) ADDRESS becomes <address> in every verb line, as mash writes it; the create and reissue synopses are the 80-column wrap with the longer word (create still fits on one line, reissue wraps the same way). (3) One footer as the last line after a blank line: Run mashctl <command> --help for a command's options. Today: usage: mashctl <verb> [args], ADDRESS, no footer. Other placeholders (prefix, path, number, n) are not changed here.

commands:

The usage line is mashctl endpoint <command> [args], which has no address in it, so no ADDRESS becomes <address> here; the command lines already write <address>. The last line, Run mashctl endpoint <command> --help for a command's options., is the footer the other help items use, and stays.

Usage: mashctl endpoint show <address> [--json]
  address  the endpoint, as owner.group.name
  --json   print the endpoint as JSON
Example:

The ADDRESS column header of endpoint list --wide stays: it is a column name. items.text:
Send a message to an endpoint.

Usage:
  mash send <address> [<message>] [options]

Examples:
  mash send acme.demo.alice "lunch at noon?"
  mash send acme.demo.alice --urgent --kind question "ready?"
  mash send acme.demo.alice --reply-to 2 "yes"
  git log -1 | mash send acme.demo.alice --kind fyi --file -

Arguments:
  address  Who to send to, as owner.group.name.
  message  The text. Leave it out to read the text from --file or from standard
           input.

Options:
  --kind <kind>         What sort of message this is. blocker, question and task
                        wake an idle recipient that has mash's wake channel on;
                        otherwise, and for result and fyi, the message arrives
                        with its next turn. Default: task. One exception: a
                        reply (--reply-to) marked question whose text has no
                        question mark and is at most 280 characters asks
                        nothing, so it is sent as fyi and the output says so.
  --urgent              Deliver at once, into a running turn where the agent
                        host allows it.
  --reply-to <number>   The number of the message in your inbox that this
                        answers. Signed, so the recipient can trust the link.
  --relay <number>      The number of a message in your inbox that this passes
                        on. Signed, so the recipient can trust the link.
  --id <key>            A key of your own. A second send with the same key to
                        the same address within two minutes stores nothing new,
                        so a retry cannot deliver twice.
  --file <path>         Read the message text from a file. Use - for standard
                        input; if nothing arrives there within 15 minutes the
                        command gives up.
  --endpoint <address>  Which endpoint to act as, as owner.group.name. Not
                        needed when only one is installed here.
  --creds <path>        The creds file to sign in with. Default: <config
                        folder>/<address>.creds.
  --server <url>        The server address. May be given more than once.
  --ca <path>           The certificate authority's certificate, when the server
                        uses its own.
  --config-dir <path>   The configuration folder. Default: ~/.config/mash.
  --detail              Print the fuller answer: after the usual line, more as
                        'label: value' lines; with --json, the fuller object.
  --json                Print the result as JSON: the same object the matching
                        MCP tool returns.
  --no-color            Never use color. Color is used only on a terminal, and
                        NO_COLOR is honored.
  -h, --help            Show help for the command.
items.note: No Global options: block: per-command help lists the options that apply to it, among its own. send reads the connection (--endpoint, --creds, --server, --ca, --config-dir), prints a fuller answer with --detail and a JSON object with --json, and honours --no-color, so all of them are listed; send's own options are today's, unchanged, with the labels re-padded to the longest. The --endpoint text drops the sentence about serve and hook, which are not this command. Today the help ends with the Global options block, the same text as mash --help, nine entries. Which options apply was read from cmd/mash/main.go: the connection options feed config.Load; the verbs without a --json form are prompt, serve and hook.

Print mail waiting for this session, in the form the agent host expects. Run by
the host after each tool call and with each prompt.

Usage:
  mash hook

Options:
  --endpoint <address>  Which endpoint to act as, as owner.group.name. Always
                        needed: a session becomes an endpoint only because
                        someone chose that.
  --creds <path>        The creds file to sign in with. Default: <config
                        folder>/<address>.creds.
  --server <url>        The server address. May be given more than once.
  --ca <path>           The certificate authority's certificate, when the server
                        uses its own.
  --config-dir <path>   The configuration folder. Default: ~/.config/mash.
  -h, --help            Show help for the command.
items.note: Two changes. (1) The Examples: entry goes: its one line, mash hook, only repeats the usage line. (2) The Global options: block goes; Options: lists what applies. hook loads the endpoint by name only (config.LoadNamedOnly), so --endpoint is listed, and it says it is always needed; --creds, --server, --ca and --config-dir feed the connection. --json is refused for hook (mash hook has no --json form) and --detail changes nothing it prints, so neither is listed; hook prints context for the host, not a terminal line, so --no-color is not either. items.text:
Run as an MCP server, which is how an agent host such as Claude Code calls
mash's tools. Started by the host, not by hand.

Usage:
  mash serve [options]

Options:
  --wake-count <n>       Wake the session when more than this many messages are
                         waiting. Default 15; 0 turns it off.
  --wake-age <duration>  Wake the session when the oldest waiting message is
                         older than this. Default 1h; 0 turns it off.
  --accept-unverified    Deliver mail that is not verified, with its trust
                         label. Default: off; such mail is refused.
  --endpoint <address>   Which endpoint to act as, as owner.group.name. Always
                         needed: a session becomes an endpoint only because
                         someone chose that.
  --creds <path>         The creds file to sign in with. Default: <config
                         folder>/<address>.creds.
  --server <url>         The server address. May be given more than once.
  --ca <path>            The certificate authority's certificate, when the
                         server uses its own.
  --config-dir <path>    The configuration folder. Default: ~/.config/mash.
  -h, --help             Show help for the command.
items.note: Three changes. (1) The description says what MCP is, in the word's first place in the help: Run as an MCP server, which is how an agent host such as Claude Code calls mash's tools. Started by the host, not by hand. Today: Run as an MCP server for an agent host. Started by the host, not by hand. The same text is mash serve's line in mash --help (help-mash-top-glossary). (2) The Examples: entry goes (it only repeated the usage line). (3) No Global options: block; --endpoint (always needed, LoadNamedOnly), --creds, --server, --ca and --config-dir are listed under Options: with serve's own three, which are unchanged. No --json (refused), --detail (nothing to detail) or --no-color (serve runs behind an agent host, not a terminal).

items.text:
Ask an endpoint a live question and wait for its answer. Not stored: if the
recipient is not there, it fails.

Usage:
  mash prompt <address> <text>

Arguments:
  address  Who to ask.
  text     The question.

Options:
  --endpoint <address>  Which endpoint to act as, as owner.group.name. Not
                        needed when only one is installed here.
  --creds <path>        The creds file to sign in with. Default: <config
                        folder>/<address>.creds.
  --server <url>        The server address. May be given more than once.
  --ca <path>           The certificate authority's certificate, when the server
                        uses its own.
  --config-dir <path>   The configuration folder. Default: ~/.config/mash.
  -h, --help            Show help for the command.
items.note: Same two changes as hook: the Examples: entry goes (mash prompt acme.demo.alice "are you there?" only restates the usage line with values) and the Global options: block becomes the options that apply. prompt has no --json form (refused), so --json is not listed; the connection options and --endpoint are. --detail is left out: prompt prints the answer and nothing fuller (not verified against a live answer here). Today: the full nine-entry block and the Examples: line.

items.text:
Make a key pair: a secret seed and its public key. For when the seed must never
leave this machine.

Usage:
  mash key create [options]

Examples:
  mash key create --out bob.seed

Options:
  --out <path>  Where to write the seed. The public key goes beside it with .pub
                added. Default: mash.seed in the current folder.
  --json        Print the result as JSON.
  -h, --help    Show help for the command.
items.note: Three changes. (1) The description says what a seed is where the word first appears: Make a key pair: a secret seed and its public key. For when the seed must never leave this machine. Today the command has two descriptions, Make a seed and its public key. here and Make your own key pair, for when the seed must never leave this machine. in mash --help; the rule says one, so this is the one, used in both. (2) The Examples: entry stays: mash key create --out bob.seed names an option, so it adds something. (3) No Global options: block. key create reads no configuration (it needs no endpoint, server or creds), so no connection option applies; --json does (it prints {"seed","public_key"}, run here) and is listed. --detail is accepted and prints nothing more, so it is not listed.

items.note: The hint goes. Today: error: no endpoint is installed here, then hint: mash join <file>. ADR 0168 wants a command that fixes it. mash join <file> does, but only for a person who already holds a join file, and the person this error meets is usually one who does not: the file is made elsewhere, by whoever runs the server, with mashctl endpoint create <address> --out <file> (docs/operations.md, Adding an endpoint; install.md). On the machine that runs mashctl the first step is a different command, mashctl endpoint create <address>, which installs the creds without any join file (same section). Two roles, two first steps, and neither can be run from here as printed, so no single command fixes it and there is no hint. If a placeholder is allowed in a hint (ADR 0168 accepted mashctl init --config <file> for the signing refusals), keep today's hint; the choice is the lead's. The other mash join <file> hints (a creds file missing, deleted, refused) are not changed: there an endpoint was installed and a join file replaces it.

The first twelve match the TO-1 rows of the Gate 1 render (#1560) byte for byte; the rest are the other malformed cases mash refuses today, which S4 adds to the spec. `not verified` is a refusal reason, not a trust kind: it is the class of a forged sender only. rules_next.rule: In --json, one name for one fact
rules_next.detail: A yes-or-no fact has one name in every command of both tools: online is a boolean wherever it appears (mash who, mash status, mashctl endpoint list and show, mashctl status), never ready, ok or state for the same fact; an endpoint's suspended state is its own boolean, suspended. ready stays the name of "mail works for this endpoint" and "the server works" (mash status and mashctl status, which was ok). A count is named as a count: endpoint_count, online_count, wake_count. An unset field is null: never "" and never left out, so a command's keys are the same on every run. An empty list is [] and an empty map is {}. A list's key is plural: capabilities, not capability, everywhere except mash who --json, whose capability ADR 0049 keeps (who JSON fields are added, never renamed or removed); that is the one named exception. A doctor row's state (ok, warn, fail, skip) is a different fact and keeps its name.

rules_next.rule: A list is a plain table
rules_next.detail: A header row in capitals, two spaces between columns, no borders. Every cell is printed on every row, so a line stands on its own and can be grepped or cut: a repeated owner or group is not left blank. A sender or an endpoint is always its full address. --wide adds columns, and may show the address in place of NAME where both would not fit in 80 (the address carries the name). When an address is long, a line may be longer than 80 columns: nothing is truncated or wrapped, so every line stays one record that grep and cut can use. The 80-column limit applies to the demo's example addresses. Example, at the 64-character maximum: Bob's address northwindtraders.platformengineering.nightlypullrequestreviewers (owner.group.name, 64 characters) is printed whole in the address column of mash inbox and of mashctl endpoint list, and those lines pass 80 columns with nothing cut. An empty list is one sentence.
rules_next.replaces: A list is a plain table

rules_next.detail: Past tense, naming the thing, with a capital first letter and no full stop, in both tools: 'Created endpoint acme.demo.bob', 'Deleted endpoint acme.demo.bob', "Mail sent (number 42 in acme.demo.alice's inbox)". It does not print what another command already shows; it does print an identifier the person can get nowhere else, and the location of a file it wrote ('Credentials: <path>').

rules_next.rule: One thing is a list of 'label: value' lines
rules_next.detail: In every block of such lines, in text and under --detail, the labels are padded to the longest label in the block plus one space, so the values start in one column, and no value begins before it.
rules_next.replaces: One thing is a list of 'label: value' lines

rules_next.rule: A wrong command line gets one error line in a fixed form, and one hint
rules_next.detail: A missing argument: 'error: mash send needs <address>'. A bad value: 'error: --kind must be one of blocker, question, task, result, fyi' or 'error: --reply-to must be a whole number'. Two things that cannot go together: 'error: mash send takes the message text or --file, not both'. A command that does not exist: 'error: unknown command "nope"', in both tools. A flag that does not exist: 'error: unknown flag --x', in both tools, wherever it stands, with no hint (ADR 0168: a hint is a command that fixes the problem, or there is none). Where there is a hint it is a command that fixes the problem, not a pointer to --help. Exit 2, and nothing is attempted.
rules_next.replaces: A wrong command line gets one error line in a fixed form, and one hint

rules_next.detail: 'error: no <thing> <value>', echoing the value as typed: 'error: no endpoint acme.demo.dave', 'error: no message 9'. The hint, when there is one, is the command that lists what exists or makes it.

rules_next.rule: --help has one layout, generated from this specification
rules_next.detail: For a command, in this order: the one-line description; 'Usage:' and the synopsis; 'Examples:'; 'Arguments:'; 'Options:'; 'Global options:'. Nothing else, 80 columns. For the tool itself: its one-line description, then one sentence that says what SAP, NATS and creds are (here and in no other help), then, for mash, one heading per group in the specification's order ('Everyday:', 'Setup:', 'Integration:', 'Raw SAP:') with each command and its one-line description indented beneath; mashctl's top-level help stays one flat list of its verbs in 0.5.10 (grouping it is not part of this item); then 'Global options:' in both tools, followed only by the configuration text that help already carries. A command is described once, in the specification, and that one description is used wherever the command is listed. Help is never written by hand beside the specification.
rules_next.replaces: --help has one layout, generated from this specification

rules_next.rule: One exit rule, the same in both tools
rules_next.detail: 0 it worked, 1 it failed, 2 the command line was wrong and nothing was attempted. This holds for every command of mash and mashctl. A command that needs another code is named here as an exception; none is left implicit. There is one exception today: mash hook exits 0 whatever happens, so that a bad configuration or a failed check never fails the session that runs it. No command exits with a code above 2. status and doctor are not exceptions: they exit 1 when they found a problem (a warning alone is 0, or 1 with --strict), as a failure does. A command that did part of its work exits 1, says what is left, and is safe to run again.
